issue: Beef stock has no key; store-bought stock/bouillon often contains celery, and some contain wheat, soy or milk.

name: polvo de hornear
issue: Baking powder has no key; most baking powders contain cornstarch (some use wheat starch).

name: aceite

name: costillas de cerdo ahumadas
issue: Smoked pork ribs have an empty key, so the pork is not tagged.

name: panza de cerdo
issue: Pork belly has an empty key, so the pork is not tagged.

name: farofa
issue: Farofa is keyed 'masa' (corn), but it is cassava flour, not corn; store-bought farofa is often toasted with butter (milk) and bacon (pork).
suggest: remove corn/masa; tag milk + pork or note to check label

name: carne seca
issue: Carne seca has no key; commercial cured/dried beef can contain sulphites or nitrites.

name: extracto de vainilla
issue: Vanilla extract has no key; standard extract is ~35% alcohol.

name: mantequilla
issue: Step 1 and blurb depend on browning milk solids; a dairy-free butter substitute will not brown the same way or smell of hazelnut, and the 'hazelnut' wording may confuse nut-allergic readers (no hazelnuts are used).
suggest: add note: 'beurre noisette' = browned butter, contains no hazelnut

name: vinagre de malta
issue: Malt vinegar has no key; it is made from barley malt and contains gluten.

name: polvo de hornear
issue: Baking powder has no key; usually contains cornstarch (sometimes wheat starch).

name: cerveza fría
issue: Blurb says the alcohol evaporates; in a 6-7 min fry not all alcohol cooks off, so this is misleading for alcohol-avoiders. Swapping to non-alcoholic beer still contains barley/gluten; sparkling water is the safe swap.
suggest: reword blurb; substitution note: sparkling water for alcohol+gluten-free

name: kirsch
issue: Kirsch has no key; it is a spirit.

name: vino blanco seco
issue: Step 6 says to slake the rescue cornstarch 'in a little wine'; someone who swapped the wine (alcohol/sulphite) needs to use their substitute liquid instead. Also the wine is only heated to steaming, so the alcohol does not cook off.
suggest: reword step 6: 'in a little of the same wine (or substitute)'

issue: Sherry vinegar has no key; wine-based vinegars typically contain sulphites.

name: aceite
issue: Frying oil unspecified; Southern fried chicken is very commonly fried in peanut oil.

name: vino shaoxing
issue: Key 'shaoxing' tags only alcohol; Shaoxing wine is brewed with wheat and usually contains salt and sometimes caramel colour/sulphites.

name: miel cruda
issue: Safety: honey (raw especially) must never be given to infants under 12 months (infant botulism). Tip 3's botulism reassurance holds only if the honey actually acidifies (pH below 4.6); raw garlic is low-acid. Consider a warning and suggest checking pH with test strips.
suggest: add infant-honey warning; soften tip 3 / suggest pH < 4.6 check

name: vinagre de vino blanco
issue: White wine vinegar has no key; wine vinegars typically contain sulphites.

name: chocolate negro
issue: Key 'darkchocolate' tags only soy; many dark chocolates contain milk fat/milk solids or carry milk cross-contact warnings.

name: pasta choux
issue: Choux pastry is keyed 'apflour' (wheat only), but choux is made with butter (or milk) and several eggs; milk and egg are not tagged from this line.

name: mostaza de Dijon
issue: Dijon mustard is correctly tagged mustard, but Dijon is usually made with white wine/verjuice and preserved with sulphites.

name: Gougères
issue: Step 2 says 'with the last egg' although the eggs are hidden inside the choux line; someone swapping egg won't see it listed. Make the choux sub-recipe explicit.
suggest: list choux components or link sub-recipe

name: agua o caldo de res
issue: Beef stock (alternative to water) has no key; store-bought stock/bouillon often contains celery, and some contain wheat, soy or milk.
suggest: celery; check label for wheat, soy, milk

name: brioche
issue: Brioche is keyed 'bread' (wheat only), but brioche is made with eggs and butter/milk.

name: aquavit o vodka
issue: Aquavit or vodka has no key; it is a spirit and is not cooked off (raw cure).

name: Gravlax
issue: Step 6 adds vinegar and oil to the sauce but neither is in the ingredient list, so their allergens (e.g. sulphites in wine vinegar) are invisible; prepared mustard also commonly contains wine vinegar/sulphites.
suggest: add vinegar + oil lines with keys; consider sulphite on mustard

name: pasta de curry verde
issue: Green curry paste is keyed only 'chilli'; traditional and most store-bought pastes contain shrimp paste (crustacean) and some contain fish sauce.

name: salami y mortadela
issue: Salami and mortadella are keyed 'pancetta' (pork only); mortadella commonly contains pistachios (tree nut), and cured sausages may contain milk powder and sulphites/nitrites.
suggest: pork, treenut (pistachio); check label for milk, sulphite

name: pepperoncini
issue: Pickled pepperoncini are keyed only 'chilli'; jarred pepperoncini are usually preserved with sodium bisulfite.

name: vinagre de vino tinto
issue: Red wine vinegar has no key; wine vinegars typically contain sulphites.

name: provolone

name: harina
issue: Blurb says there is 'no substitute that works' for the flour roux; for a wheat/gluten allergy a dark roux made with sweet rice or sorghum flour does work (browns faster). The absolute wording may push people to skip the dish or use flour unsafely.
suggest: soften blurb; add GF roux substitution note

name: mostaza en grano
issue: Whole-grain mustard has an EMPTY key, so this mustard is not tagged; someone avoiding mustard who swaps the two keyed mustards would still get it.

name: mostaza de Dijon
issue: Dijon mustard is tagged mustard only; Dijon is usually made with white wine/verjuice and preserved with sulphites.

name: ajo
issue: Safety: the optional raw garlic clove steeped in honey stored at room temperature for months is a botulism risk (low-acid garlic in an anaerobic medium); the 2 tbsp vinegar may not acidify enough. Either strain the garlic out and refrigerate, or drop the room-temperature storage claim when garlic is used.
suggest: add note: if using garlic, strain it out or refrigerate and use within a few weeks
